A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bellman-unbiasedness framework and SF-LSVI algorithm. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite the revised title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees, proofs, and analytical examples. Its tables and figures contain theoretical comparisons, notation, and illustrations, not original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper, including its appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Normalized-moment regression, confidence-width bonuses, and greedy planning are retained. Algorithm 1 moves from v1 Section 5 to v2 Appendix B; its state-argument notation correction does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmarks for training or evaluation. Both study the same theoretical finite-horizon MDP framework.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains O-DISCO and V-EST-LSR as theoretical comparators; the revised columns do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. The episodic interaction setup and expected-return regret objective remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. The added variance and Gaussian-mixture examples are mathematical or explanatory illustrations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance testing. The retained confidence bounds and new variance-estimator example concern theoretical reasoning, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. Table 1 and the corresponding regret theorems retain the same guarantees, including the advertised O-tilde(d_E H^(3/2) sqrt(K)) bound.

T1.justification: v1 Assumption 4.9 bounds approximation error in the finite sketch class; v2 Definition 3.8 instead defines full-distribution misspecification through an infimum-supremum expression. v2 also adds explicit mean-variance estimation and variance-homogeneity formulas, and restricts the quantile level from [0,1] to (0,1) in the proof of Lemma C.2. The central theorems and appendix proof arguments are retained; the new variance formulas contain errors.

C1.justification: Both versions claim moment-sketch uniqueness, statistical-functional Bellman completeness, and the same SF-LSVI regret guarantee. v2 emphasizes online learning more explicitly without changing the underlying contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument against separating policy learning from distribution estimation through extra rollouts, citing sample costs, accumulated approximation error, and limited reuse across policies. Section 3.2 also elaborates why unbiasedness without closedness cannot sustain the update process.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, moment normalization, regression specification, and computational caveat about confidence-width optimization are retained, with the latter moved to Appendix B. No substantive implementation or code/data-access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jin et al. (2021) and Agarwal et al. (2023), revises moment-problem references, and removes several v1 bibliography entries. Its principal positioning relative to Rowland et al., O-DISCO, and V-EST-LSR remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction and statistical-functional discussion are substantially rewritten and reorganized. Bellman closedness and unbiasedness receive separate subsections, explanatory passages are expanded, and pseudocode and technical remarks move into a new Appendix B. The title changes, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column main paper with extensively reformatted displays. Figure 1 gains revised annotations and caption; Table 1 replaces its tractability column with separate finite-representation and exact-learnability columns. The existing two diagrams in v1 Figure 3 receive separate captions and a combined caption in v2; Algorithm 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization and explains the framework more explicitly, but introduces mathematical errors into its central unbiasedness examples. Section 3.2 equates variance with E[(Z1-Z2)^2], which equals twice the variance for independent identically distributed draws, and its purported unbiased estimator uses an uncorrected sample-variance term. These errors weaken explanatory correctness and outweigh the limited clarity gains, while the algorithm, headline guarantees, and principal appendix proofs remain unchanged.
